settlement_source: Source Agency = United States Congress (swearing-in/certificate of election presented to Senate)
settlement_variable: Party of the first candidate who presents a certificate of election and is sworn into the U.S. Senate for Maine seat, term beginning 2027
rounding: n/a (categorical outcome; $1.00 settlement value, min tick per contract terms)
trading_close_vs_settlement: Last Trading Time = Expiration Time; Expiration = sooner of first 10:00 AM ET after swearing-in or 1 year after popular vote; settlement within a day unless under review
early_close_or_void_clauses: Accelerated resolution when >=4 of 8 Designated Media Sources (NYT, AP, DDHQ, CNN, Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC) call a winner with none contradicting; 'unambiguous statement in a news article' counts; affiliate call can represent network; Exchange may replace a source at its sole discretion. Vacancy -> party of first replacement sworn in. Kalshi Market Outcome Review at sole discretion.
title_vs_rules_divergences: Title 'win the Senate race in Maine' vs rules 'sworn in' for term beginning 2027 - settlement formally Jan 2027 unless accelerated
Maine uses ranked-choice voting for federal general elections: winner may not be known until RCV tabulation, delaying calls (not stated in rules)
Independent caucusing with a party: contract treats 'Independent' as a separate value; party on election day
yes_sub_title names candidates (Collins/Jackson) but resolves on party

RCV tabulation delay increases risk of contradictory media calls vs. accelerated clause
